text: The tokenizer rule that takes the longest character run which could form a token — so that `123` is one number and not three — is called ___ munch.
explanation: It is why scanning forward while characters keep qualifying is the right loop, and why `x1` is a single name while `1x` produces `NUMBER(1)` followed by `NAME(x)` rather than an error. Tokenizers are usually permissive that way; rejecting `1x` is the parser's job, and keeping the split clean is part of why the two passes are separate.
